applies_why: Yes: the judge uses the cited texts' non-statement that Joseph begat the child as part of the ground for holding the defense/STANDS.
quote: neither text states that Joseph begat the child ([L4]). Because the defender answered the witnesses pressed against the chain and neither withdrew nor suffered refutation of the declared links, the defense holds ([L4]).
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: 'single verse does not state a link or its contrary' — I weighed a broad reading covering the cited texts' non-statement used to uphold a STANDS result against a narrow reading limited to an expressly one-verse silence.
why: The judge relies on the cited texts' not stating that Joseph begat the child to support a defense-holds/STANDS outcome, which is the non-statement ground K-S2 forbids.
